mainTopic: Feeding tests for eye blemishes, blemishes of the nose, lip and gums, and whether a limb missing inside the body disqualifies a קרבן
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of questions about how to feed a בכור whose eye blemish is being tested. Each question has one side that clearly works and one side that is unclear. The questions ask whether the feeding happens at every meal, before or after eating and drinking, with the animal tied or untied, alone or with another animal, and in the city or the field. רב אשי adds a question about a garden near the city, and all of these end in תיקו. רב נחמן בר יצחק says that the three checks of רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס must be evenly spaced. פנחס asks שמואל whether a blemish confirmed by the three-month test counts from the beginning or only from then on, which matters for מעילה with redemption money. שמואל has no answer and praises the question. New משניות list blemishes of the nose, lip and gums, and the גמרא explains that only blemishes that can be seen count. It also fills in missing words in a ברייתא about the double teeth, which brings out three different opinions. Finally, רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether a limb missing inside the body makes an animal unfit for the altar. The גמרא tests this with two ברייתות about an animal with one kidney and works through several ways to reconcile them, ending with a challenge to רבי יוחנן's answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the fodder given at every meal?
steps.stepSummary: The question offers a second option: perhaps the animal must be fed the fig-sized amount at every meal, not just once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is fed this way at each and every meal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that began just before this. It asks whether the animal gets the measured fodder only at the first meal, or at every meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is fed a fig-sized amount of fodder to see whether its eye spot clears up. The question is whether one such feeding is enough for the test, or whether it must be repeated at every meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)
Meal, here a feeding of the animal

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of a question that started before this section. The first half asked about only the first meal.

phrases.english: Or perhaps at each and every meal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the test feeding must happen at every meal or only at the first meal

steps.title: Before eating or after eating?
steps.stepSummary: Even if only the first meal counts, is the fodder given before the animal's regular food or after it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is at the first meal, is it before eating or after eating? Before eating, it surely works for it like a medicine. After eating, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a follow-up question on top of the first one. It says that before the meal clearly works, and asks only about after the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Medicine is taken on an empty stomach, so fodder given before the meal surely has its full effect. After a full meal it may not work as well, so it is unclear whether the test is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (introduces a follow-up question that assumes one answer)
It is effective / good for it

phrases.english: If you say at the first meal,
is it before eating or after eating?

phrases.aramaic: קוֹדֶם אֲכִילָה וַדַּאי מְעַלֵּי לֵיהּ כְּסַמָּא,
phrases.english: Before eating, it is certainly effective for it, like a medicine;
after eating, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question that assumes the first-meal side of step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether feeding after the animal's meal is a valid test

steps.title: Before drinking or after drinking?
steps.stepSummary: A parallel question about drinking: before drinking surely works, but what about after?
steps.simpleTranslation: Before drinking or after drinking? Before drinking it surely works for it, like barley. After drinking, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about drinking instead of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals are normally fed barley before they drink, so giving the fodder before drinking clearly works. After drinking is the unclear case.

phrases.english: Before drinking or after drinking?

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹדֶם שְׁתִיָּה וַדַּאי מְעַלֵּי לֵיהּ כִּשְׂעָרֵי,
phrases.english: Before drinking, it is certainly effective for it, like barley;
after drinking, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question, moving from eating to drinking
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether feeding after drinking is a valid test

steps.title: Tied or untied?
steps.stepSummary: Is the animal fed while tied up or while free? Free surely works; tied is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tied or untied? Untied, it surely works for it. Tied, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the animal's physical state during the feeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A free animal is relaxed, so the fodder works well. A tied animal may be stressed, and it is not clear whether the fodder still has its full effect.

phrases.english: Tied or untied?
Untied, it is certainly effective for it;
tied, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the same list, now about the animal's condition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether feeding a tied animal is a valid test

steps.title: Alone or with another animal?
steps.stepSummary: With a companion surely works; alone is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alone or with another? With another, it surely works for it. Alone, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the animal must be fed with company.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal eating with another is comfortable and eats well, so the test clearly works. Alone, it might not eat in the same way, so the law is unclear.

phrases.english: By itself or with another?
With another, it is certainly effective for it;
by itself, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the same list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether feeding an animal by itself is a valid test

steps.title: In the city or in the field?
steps.stepSummary: In the field surely works; in the city is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the city or in the field? In the field, it surely works for it. In the city, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the place of feeding matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the field the animal is calm, so the fodder clearly works. The noise of the city might reduce the effect.

phrases.english: In the city or in the field?
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'and in the field' in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, reads 'or in the field.'

phrases.english: In the field, it is certainly effective for it;
in the city, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the same list, now about location
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether feeding in the city is a valid test

steps.title: A garden next to the city
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: if only the field works, what about a garden right next to the city?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If you say only in the field, what about a garden next to the city?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds one more question that builds on the city-or-field question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garden near the city sits in between. It is open like a field but close to the city's noise, so it is unclear which side it belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: A garden next to the city

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If you say only in the field,
what about a garden next to the city?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר בַּשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up that assumes the field side of step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a garden near the city counts as a field or as the city

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: All of these questions are left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the whole list of questions with תיקו: no answer was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each question had one clear side and one unclear side. The unclear sides stay unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: For each question, the clear option (before eating, before drinking, untied, with a companion, in the field) surely works. The other options, and רב אשי's garden, are left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.
phrases.notes: This covers all the questions above, not just רב אשי's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of questions without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about how to feed the animal remain unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: The three checks must be evenly spaced
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, רב נחמן בר יצחק says the three checks of רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס must be divided into equal thirds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס says (check three times within eighty days). רב נחמן בר יצחק said: provided they are divided into thirds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the opinion of רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a condition to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס says the animal is checked three times within eighty days. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that the checks must be spaced evenly, with equal gaps between them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes the check precise: the three checks cannot be bunched together but must be spread evenly across the eighty days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Antigonus says.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here: he says to check the animal three times within eighty days.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Provided that they are divided into thirds.
phrases.notes: He means the three checks must have equal gaps between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and begins a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three checks within eighty days must be evenly spaced.

steps.title: Does a failed test make the blemish count from the start?
steps.stepSummary: פנחס asks שמואל: if the animal finishes the fodder test and is not healed, is it a מום from the beginning (למפרע) or only from now on?
steps.simpleTranslation: פנחס, the brother of מר שמואל, asked שמואל: If the animal ate the test fodder and was not healed, is it a blemish going back to the beginning, or a blemish only from now on?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about the three-month test for an animal whose eyes keep tearing. Once the test shows the animal is not healed, when does the blemish start to count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a tearing eye is checked by feeding the animal moist and dry fodder for three months. If it is not healed, it is a מום. פנחס asks whether the test only reveals a מום that existed all along (למפרע), or whether the מום becomes official only once the test ends (מיכן ולהבא).

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (introduces an open question)

phrases.english: Pinchas asked
the brother of Mar Shmuel, of Shmuel:
If it ate and was not healed,
phrases.notes: "Ate" means it went through the משנה's three-month test of moist and dry fodder.

phrases.english: is it a blemish going back to the beginning,
or is it a blemish from now on?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ פִּנְחָס, אֲחוּהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל, מִשְּׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's test for tearing eyes and asks a new timing question about it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מום confirmed by the three-month test counts from the start of the test or only from its end.

steps.title: The practical difference: misusing the redemption money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question matters for מעילה with money used to redeem the animal during the test period.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Whether one commits מעילה with its redemption money. If the blemish counts from the beginning, he commits מעילה. If it counts only from now on, he does not commit מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why פנחס's question matters, and answers with a practical case about redemption money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a consecrated animal was redeemed during the three months and someone used the money. If the מום counts from the beginning, the redemption worked, the money is holy, and using it is מעילה. If the מום counts only from now on, the animal was still unblemished and could not be redeemed, so the money stayed ordinary and there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
Misusing holy property / he misuses it
Redemption (exchanging a holy item for money)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the animal is blemished. Everyone agrees it is. The question is only from when the blemish counts.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For misusing its redemption money.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְמַפְרֵעַ הָוֵי מוּמָא — מָעֵיל,
phrases.english: If you say it is a blemish going back to the beginning, he misuses it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי מִיכָּן וּלְהַבָּא הָוֵי מוּמָא — לָא מָעֵיל,
phrases.english: but if it is a blemish from now on, he does not misuse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in step 10 has real consequences.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is מעילה with redemption money given during the test period.

steps.title: שמואל has no answer and praises his brother's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is, and שמואל answers only by quoting a פסוק about the lame taking the prey. The question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? שמואל read this verse about him: "The lame take the prey."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final law, but שמואל gives no ruling. Instead he quotes a פסוק to praise his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With "the lame take the prey," שמואל is saying that even someone less learned can catch a question so sharp that he himself cannot answer it. So the question is left unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a מום confirmed by the three-month test counts from the beginning or only from now on is left unanswered. This affects מעילה with redemption money.

phrases.english: What is the law? Shmuel read about him:
"The lame take the prey."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:23. He means that someone less learned asked a question he himself couldn't answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from steps 10–11 without a ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no answer. The question stays open, and שמואל praises it as unusually sharp.

steps.title: New משנה: blemishes of the nose and lip
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more blemishes: a nose that was pierced, damaged, or split, and a lip that was pierced, damaged, or split.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Its nose that was pierced, damaged, or split. Its lip that was pierced, damaged, or split.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, continuing the list of blemishes that allow a בכור to be slaughtered outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each body part, the nose and then the lip, gets three kinds of damage: a hole (ניקב), a missing piece (נפגם), or a crack (נסדק). Any one of these counts as a מום.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Its nose that was pierced,
or that was damaged, or that was split.
Its lip that was pierced,
that was damaged, or that was split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving on from the eye blemishes to the nose and lip.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nose or lip that is pierced, damaged, or split is a מום.

steps.title: A pierced nose counts only if the hole shows on the outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה's case of a pierced nose: if the nostrils were pierced into each other, it is a מום only when the hole can be seen from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if the two nostrils were pierced into each other, and you can see it from the outside, it is a blemish. If you can only see it from the inside, it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain the משנה's case of a nose that was pierced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said a pierced nose is a blemish. The ברייתא narrows this down: the hole between the nostrils must be visible from outside. A hole that shows only on the inside is not a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: On the outside, where it can be seen
On the inside, where it is hidden

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
If its nostrils were pierced one into the other —
if it shows on the outside, this is a blemish;
if it shows only on the inside, it is not a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִיקְּבוּ חֳוטָמִין זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first case in the משנה quoted in step 13 (a pierced nose).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole between the nostrils is a מום only if it can be seen from outside.

steps.title: The lip case means the outer edge of the lip
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה's pierced, damaged or split lip refers to the outer, front part of the lip.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the lip that was pierced, damaged or split, רב פפא says: this means the outer row of the lip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's lip case, and רב פפא explains which part of the lip is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the nose case counted only the outside, רב פפא limits the lip case to the outer, sticking-out part of the lip. Damage there can be seen, so it counts as a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer row; the front edge

phrases.english: Its lip that was pierced, or damaged, or split:
Rav Pappa said:
This means the outer row of its lip.

steps.whatToRemember: For both nose and lip, the blemish must be on the outside part that can be seen.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תּוֹרָא בָּרָא דְּשִׂיפְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the second case in the same משנה (the lip).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lip blemish refers to the outer, front part of the lip.

steps.title: New משנה: damaged gums, and no checking of the double teeth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds blemishes of the gums. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says we do not check from the double teeth inward, and not even the double teeth themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Outer gums that were damaged or scratched, and inner gums that were pulled out, are blemishes. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: we do not check from the double teeth and further in, and not even the double teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה lists more blemishes in the mouth. It also gives רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's limit on how far into the mouth we look.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the outer gums, being damaged or scratched is enough. The inner gums count only if they were pulled out. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס adds that the double teeth and everything behind them are too far in to be checked, so damage there does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The double teeth: large back teeth that look like two teeth

phrases.english: MISHNA: The outer gums that were damaged,
or that were scratched,
and the inner ones that were pulled out.
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
We do not check from the double teeth and inward,
and not even the double teeth themselves.

steps.whyThisMatters: A hidden blemish does not let us slaughter a בכור, so we need to know where in the mouth a blemish still counts.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה continuing the list of blemishes, now inside the mouth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaged outer gums and pulled inner gums are blemishes. According to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, the double teeth and what lies behind them are not checked.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the double teeth, with three opinions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what the double teeth are, then says the double teeth count like the inside. רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי allows slaughter only for the outer teeth. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס ignores the double teeth completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the double teeth — what are the double teeth? From the double teeth inward, and the double teeth themselves count as inside. רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי says: we slaughter only for the outer ones. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: we pay no attention to the double teeth at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three opinions about the double teeth. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the תנא קמא) treats the double teeth like the hidden inside, so a blemish there does not allow slaughter. רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי allows slaughter only for the outer teeth. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says not to consider the double teeth at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is it? What is meant?
We slaughter (the בכור because of a blemish)
We pay attention to, take into account

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
The double teeth — what are the double teeth?
From the double teeth and inward,
and the double teeth themselves are like the inside.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefutzai says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶלָּא עַל הַחִיצוֹנוֹת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: We slaughter only for the outer ones alone.
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין עַל הַתְּיוֹמֶת כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: We pay no attention to the double teeth at all.

steps.confusionAlert: Line 2 asks 'what are the double teeth?' but the next line does not really give a definition. That is exactly what the גמרא will question next.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the תיומת mentioned in the משנה of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double teeth count as the inside of the mouth. רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי allows slaughter only for the outer teeth. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס ignores the double teeth entirely.

steps.title: The ברייתא is unclear and seems to repeat itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, since it asks a question without answering it. It also points out that רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי seems to say the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying? And also, רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי says the same thing as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises two problems with the ברייתא from step 17. Answering them is the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First problem: the ברייתא asks 'what are the double teeth?' but never really answers. Second problem: the תנא קמא says the double teeth count as inside, and רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי allows only the outer teeth. Both treat the double teeth as hidden, so why list them as two separate opinions?

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (the meaning is unclear)
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: What is it saying?
And furthermore,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹצַאי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefutzai is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording and structure of the ברייתא brought in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא about the double teeth (step 17)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא asks a question it does not answer. It also gives רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי a separate opinion that seems the same as the תנא קמא's, since both treat the double teeth as a hidden area.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words: what the inner gums are
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא has missing words. Filled in, it defines the inner gums as the double teeth and inward. Damage there does not allow slaughter, but if the teeth were uprooted, one may slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some words are missing from the ברייתא, and this is what it teaches: Which are the inner gums? From the double teeth and inward, and the double teeth themselves count as inside. When does this rule apply? When they were damaged or scratched. But if they were uprooted, we do slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18 by saying the ברייתא is missing words, and it fills them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words added, the question 'what are the double teeth?' becomes 'what are the inner gums?', and the ברייתא answers it: from the double teeth inward. It also adds a new detail. Damage to the inner gums does not allow slaughter, but uprooted teeth do allow it, according to the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the text; the גמרא fills them in
The inner part of the gums
Were uprooted or pulled out completely

steps.confusionAlert: 'Uprooted' (נעקרו) is treated more seriously than 'damaged'. For the תנא קמא, even inner teeth that were uprooted allow slaughter.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
Which are the inner ones?
From the double teeth and inward,
and the double teeth themselves count as inside.
In what case is this said?
Where they were damaged or scratched,
but if they were uprooted, we slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first part of step 18's difficulty, the question in the ברייתא that had no answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to ask what the double teeth are without giving an answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא asks what the inner gums are and answers: from the double teeth inward. Uprooted inner teeth allow slaughter.

steps.title: How רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס differ
steps.stepSummary: Filled in, the ברייתא shows that רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי disagrees with the תנא קמא. Uprooted inner teeth do not allow slaughter, but they do make the animal unfit for the altar. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says the double teeth do not matter at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי says: We slaughter only for the outer teeth. But inner teeth that were uprooted do not allow slaughter, though they do make the animal unfit. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: We pay no attention to the double teeth at all, and they do not even make the animal unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues filling in the ברייתא. This answers the second difficulty: רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי really does say something different from the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows slaughter when inner teeth are uprooted. רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי does not allow slaughter in that case, but he agrees the animal is unfit for the altar. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס goes further: a blemish on the double teeth means nothing at all, not even unfitness.

keyTerms.meaning: It does become unfit for the altar
We pay no attention to it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. Allowed to slaughter (תנא קמא, for uprooted inner teeth). Not allowed to slaughter but unfit for the altar (רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי). No effect at all on the double teeth (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefutzai says:
We slaughter only for the outer teeth,
but inner ones that were uprooted,
we do not slaughter for them,
but it does become unfit.
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין עַל הַתְּיוֹמֶת כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: We pay no attention to the double teeth at all,
and it does not even become unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹצַאי אוֹמֵר: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶלָּא עַל הַחִיצוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the filled-in ברייתא and answers the second part of step 18's difficulty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי seemed to say the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He disagrees about uprooted inner teeth. They do not allow slaughter, but they do make the animal unfit.

steps.title: Does a limb missing on the inside count?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether a limb missing inside the body counts as a מחוסר אבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked: Does a missing limb on the inside count as a missing limb, or does it not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether an internal missing limb counts as a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about teeth and gums. This question is broader: if a limb is missing inside the body, where no one can see it, does it count as missing?

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question he is unsure about
Missing a limb, which is a type of blemish
On the inside of the body

phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami asked:
Is there such a thing as a missing limb on the inside,
or is there no such thing as a missing limb on the inside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected by the theme of blemishes that cannot be seen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a limb missing inside the body counts as a מחוסר אבר.

steps.title: What could the question be about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the question is about. For a בכור, and for other קדשים, the פסוקים list only blemishes that can be seen, so an internal blemish clearly does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose? If for a בכור, it is written 'lame or blind.' If for קדשים, it is written 'blind or broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. Both possible uses seem to have a clear answer already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about a בכור and about קדשים list blemishes that are easy to see. So an internal blemish could not allow slaughtering a בכור or redeeming קדשים. That makes it unclear what רב אחדבוי בר אמי was unsure about.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose? What is the practical difference?
'Lame or blind', the פסוק about a בכור
'Blind or broken', the פסוק about קדשים

phrases.english: For what? If for a firstborn,
it is written 'lame or blind,'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:21. Both are blemishes you can see from the outside.

phrases.english: if for sacrificial animals,
it is written 'blind or broken'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 21's question could be about.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים already show that only visible blemishes count, so there seems to be nothing to ask.

steps.title: The question is only about making the animal unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question is not about slaughtering or redeeming. It is only about whether an internal missing limb makes the animal unfit for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: We did not ask about slaughtering or redeeming. What we asked about is making the animal unfit: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question. It is asking about one specific result, disqualifying the animal from the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that the פסוקים settle slaughtering a בכור and redeeming קדשים. An internal blemish cannot allow those. But whether it at least makes the animal unfit for the altar is still open. This matches the middle level from step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: For slaughtering a בכור outside the בית המקדש because of a blemish
For making the animal unfit for the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a blemish can have a middle level. It may be too weak to allow slaughter or redemption but still strong enough to disqualify the animal from the altar.

phrases.english: About slaughtering and redeeming
we did not have a question,
where we have a question is about making it unfit: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by narrowing the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to be about slaughtering or redeeming, which the פסוקים already settle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is only whether an internal missing limb makes the animal unfit for the altar.

steps.title: The two sides of the question about internal missing limbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both ways of reading the פסוק. Either תמים means whole inside and out, or it is limited, like a מום, to the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says 'It shall be complete to be accepted.' Complete, yes; lacking, no. Or perhaps we read 'complete to be accepted' together with 'there shall be no blemish in it.' Just as a blemish is on the outside, so too a lack only counts on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible sides of רב אחדבוי בר אמי's question, now that we know it is only about fitness for the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says תמים is a full requirement, so anything missing, even inside, disqualifies. Side two says the same פסוק goes on to talk about a מום, and a מום is something seen on the outside. So a 'lack' should also be limited to the outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete, whole; the Torah's requirement for a קרבן
A lack; something missing from the animal
Or perhaps; introduces the other side of a question

phrases.english: "It shall be complete to be accepted," says the Merciful One,
complete, yes; lacking, no.
Or perhaps, "It shall be complete to be accepted,"
"there shall be no blemish in it":
just as a blemish is on the outside,
so too a lack is only on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question that step 23 narrowed down to fitness for the altar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the word תמים a full requirement, so even an internal lack disqualifies, or is it limited by the nearby word מום to outside lacks only?

steps.title: Two ברייתות about an animal with one kidney
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two ברייתות. One rules out an animal with one kidney and the other includes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And the two kidneys' means not an animal with one kidney and not one with three kidneys. Another ברייתא teaches: 'He shall remove it' comes to include an animal with one kidney.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins an attempt to answer the question from sources about kidneys. It first sets up two ברייתות that seem to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kidney is an internal organ, so a missing kidney is a perfect test case for an internal lack. The first ברייתא disqualifies an animal with one kidney. The second ברייתא learns from the singular word יסירנה that such an animal is fine.

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And the two kidneys":
but not an animal with one kidney,
and not an animal with three kidneys.
And another ברייתא teaches: "He shall remove it":
to include an animal with one kidney.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings sources to try to settle the question laid out in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an internal lack counts as a lack
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות on ויקרא 3:4 that disagree about an animal with one kidney

steps.title: Suggesting the ברייתות argue about internal lacks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes no animal is born with one kidney, so the two ברייתות must argue about whether an internal lack counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed everyone agrees that no animal is created with one kidney, so this one must have lost one. So let us say this is what they argue about: one holds that an internal lack is called a lack, and the other holds that an internal lack is not called a lack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two ברייתות would answer our question. It turns them into a disagreement between תנאים on exactly this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting assumption is that a one-kidney animal must have lost a kidney. Then the only way to explain the two ברייתות is that they disagree about internal lacks. The first ברייתא says it counts, and the second says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature as it was naturally created
Let us say this is what they argue about

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is the final answer. It rests on the assumption that no animal is born with one kidney, and the next step rejects that assumption.

phrases.english: They assumed that everyone agrees
there is no creature created with one kidney,
since this one surely became lacking.
Let us say this is what they argue about:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר, חֶסְרוֹן מִבִּפְנִים שְׁמֵיהּ חֶסְרוֹן,
phrases.english: that one master holds an internal lack is called a lack,
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, which disqualifies the one-kidney animal.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר, חֶסְרוֹן מִבִּפְנִים לָא שְׁמֵיהּ חֶסְרוֹן.
phrases.english: and the other master holds an internal lack is not called a lack.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין בְּרִיָּה בְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the two ברייתות in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That internal lack is a question argued by תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two ברייתות, read with the assumption that no animal is born with one kidney

steps.title: רב חייא בר יוסף: born with one kidney versus losing one
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר יוסף says everyone agrees an internal lack counts. The ברייתות deal with different cases: an animal that lost a kidney, and one born with only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר יוסף said: Everyone agrees an animal can be created with one kidney, and that an internal lack is called a lack. It is not difficult. Here, it was created with two and lost one. There, it was created with one from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר יוסף rejects the idea that the ברייתות argue. He explains each one as talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He drops the earlier assumption and says an animal can be born with one kidney. Such an animal is not missing anything, so it is fit, as in the second ברייתא. An animal that lost one of its two kidneys is lacking, and since everyone agrees an internal lack counts, it is unfit, as in the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult; the sources do not contradict

steps.whatToRemember: רב חייא בר יוסף's split (born with one kidney is fit, lost a kidney is unfit) is challenged in the next step. The גמרא then replaces it in step 29. What survives is his point that an internal lack counts as a lack.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'lacking' is measured against how the animal itself was created, not against a standard animal.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Yosef said:
Everyone agrees there is a creature created with one kidney,
and an internal lack is called a lack,
and it is not difficult:
here, when it was created with two and they became lacking,
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, which disqualifies the animal.

phrases.english: there, when it was created with one from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ בְּרִיָּה בְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 26's claim that the ברייתות argue about internal lacks.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two ברייתות are a disagreement between תנאים about internal lacks.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that no animal is born with one kidney is wrong. Once it is dropped, the ברייתות are about two different cases and do not argue.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed at this point: everyone agrees an internal lack disqualifies, and the ברייתות split between an animal born with one kidney and one that lost a kidney. The split is challenged in step 28 and replaced in step 29.

steps.title: One kidney is listed next to three kidneys, so both are from birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חייא בר יוסף. The first ברייתא lists one kidney together with three kidneys. Three kidneys must be from birth, so one kidney must also be from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches one kidney in the same breath as three kidneys! Just as three kidneys are there from the very start, so too one kidney is from the very start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חייא בר יוסף, who said the first ברייתא is about an animal that lost a kidney later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal cannot grow an extra kidney, so the case of three kidneys must be from birth. The ברייתא puts one kidney right beside three kidneys, so the two cases should be alike. That means the one-kidney animal in the first ברייתא was born that way, and רב חייא בר יוסף's split falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to, in the same style as

phrases.english: But it teaches it as similar to three [kidneys],
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא from step 25, the one that rules out an animal with one kidney.

phrases.english: just as three are from the start,
so too one is from the start!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רב חייא בר יוסף from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חייא בר יוסף's claim that the first ברייתא is about an animal that lost a kidney later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cases listed side by side should be alike. Three kidneys can only come from birth, so one kidney must also be from birth.

steps.title: The argument is whether an animal can be born with one kidney
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reading. The תנאים argue about whether an animal can naturally be born with one kidney. One says it can, so the animal is not lacking anything. The other says it cannot, so the animal is missing a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they argue about whether such a creature exists from birth. One Sage holds that a creature can be born with one kidney. The other Sage holds that no creature is born with one kidney.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב חייא בר יוסף's split did not work, the גמרא offers a new explanation of the two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides still agree that an internal missing part counts as a lack. The new argument is about nature. If animals can be born with one kidney, this animal is complete and allowed. If they cannot, this animal is missing a kidney and is unfit. This overturns the assumption in step 26 that everyone agrees no animal is born with one kidney.

keyTerms.meaning: a creature, a natural form something can be created in
one Sage holds... and the other Sage holds

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּיֵשׁ בְּרִיָּה מֵעִיקָּרָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: Rather, here they disagree about whether such a creature exists from the start,
one Sage holds: there is a creature with one [kidney],
and one Sage holds: there is no creature with one [kidney].

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the argument from step 26. There, the question was whether an internal lack counts. Here, everyone agrees it counts, and the only argument is whether an animal can be born with one kidney.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּיֵשׁ בְּרִיָּה מֵעִיקָּרָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected split from step 27 after the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a new point: whether an animal can be born with one kidney.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות argued about whether an internal lack counts, or dealt with an animal born with one kidney versus one that lost a kidney.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees an internal lack counts. The argument is whether an animal can naturally be born with one kidney.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: losing the kidney before or after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees no animal is born with one kidney, and everyone agrees an internal lack counts. The first ברייתא is about an animal that lost the kidney before שחיטה, so it is unfit. The second is about one that lost it after שחיטה, so it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: everyone agrees no creature is born with one kidney, and an inner lack counts as a lack. Still, there is no problem. Here, the kidney was lost before שחיטה. There, it was lost after שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers a different way to fit the two ברייתות together, without any argument between the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן keeps both assumptions: no animal is born with one kidney, and an internal lack counts. He explains the two ברייתות by timing. What matters is when the kidney went missing. Before שחיטה it makes the animal unfit, but after שחיטה it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: a lack on the inside, an internal missing part
here... there (one case versus the other)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
everyone agrees there is no creature with one [kidney],
and a lack on the inside is called a lack.
And it is not difficult:
here, where it lost [the kidney] before slaughter,
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, the one that rules the animal out.

phrases.english: there, where it lost [the kidney] after slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֲמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין בְּרִיָּה בְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from step 29, explaining the ברייתות as two different cases instead of an argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by when the kidney was lost: before שחיטה or after שחיטה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות must be arguing with each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: No argument. A kidney lost before שחיטה makes the animal unfit, and one lost after שחיטה does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings in timing. The question becomes when the animal had to be whole, which sets up the next challenge.

steps.title: Is a kidney lost after slaughter but before collecting the blood really allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. If the kidney was lost after שחיטה but before the blood was collected, is the animal really allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was lost after שחיטה but before קבלה, is it permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's line between before and after שחיטה. It points to the time between שחיטה and catching the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The work of a קרבן is not finished at שחיטה. The blood still has to be collected in a vessel, which is called קבלה. The גמרא asks: if the kidney went missing in that window, why should the animal be allowed? This makes רבי יוחנן's line at שחיטה look too early.

keyTerms.meaning: collecting the blood in a holy vessel

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה קוֹדֶם קַבָּלָה מִי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: And after slaughter but before collecting [the blood], is it permitted?
phrases.notes: The question expects the answer no, because the קרבן's service isn't finished yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה קוֹדֶם קַבָּלָה מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that losing a kidney after שחיטה leaves the animal allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal must stay whole until קבלה, so a kidney lost between שחיטה and קבלה should still make it unfit. Drawing the line at שחיטה seems wrong.
